unit.title: Media planning and marketing budget
unit.description: Reach, frequency, GRP, effective frequency, media mix, MER, blended CAC, incrementality, marketing mix modeling, zero-base budget

cards.definition: The document that says where, when, how often and with which budget a campaign runs: channels, formats, targeting, flighting (calendar), expected reach and frequency, and how results will be measured.
cards.example: Four weeks: YouTube and connected TV for reach, Meta for frequency, search to capture demand, with weekly budgets.

cards.definition: Reach in percent of the target multiplied by average frequency. 60 percent of the target reached 3 times on average gives 180 GRP. It measures pressure, not quality.
cards.example: A TV plan of 300 GRP on women aged 25 to 49.

cards.definition: The number of exposures needed for a message to be noticed and remembered, often estimated between 3 and 10 depending on creative, category and competition. Beyond a point, extra exposures waste money and annoy.
cards.example: Capping display ads at 5 impressions per person per week.

cards.definition: Continuous plans run all year at a steady level; flighting runs bursts with pauses; pulsing keeps a low base with peaks. Choice depends on seasonality and budget.
cards.example: A toy brand concentrates spend in November and December, with a light presence the rest of the year.

cards.definition: Statistical models estimating the contribution of each channel to sales from aggregated data (spend, sales, seasonality, price), without cookies. Open-source tools like Meta Robyn and Google Meridian made it accessible; it is best combined with incrementality tests.
cards.example: An MMM shows TV adds sales for weeks after airing, which last-click attribution never credited.

exercises.prompt: A plan reaches 50 percent of the target with an average frequency of 4. How many GRP?
exercises.explain: GRP = reach percent x average frequency = 50 x 4. It describes pressure, not whether people remembered the ad.

exercises.prompt: Which pair of figures should a media plan give?
choices: Reach and frequency on the target
Followers and likes on the page
Clicks and bounce rate only
Number of ads and number of colours
exercises.explain: How many people of the target will see the message, and how many times. Then the measure of results.

exercises.prompt: Your display ads were shown 25 times per person in a week. What do you do?
choices: Cap frequency and widen the reach
Raise the bid to show them more
Change nothing while clicks come in
Show the ads only to past buyers
exercises.explain: Beyond effective frequency, extra impressions annoy and waste budget. A cap frees money to reach new people.

exercises.prompt: A toy brand spends 70 percent of its budget in November and December. Which scheduling is it?
choices: Flighting around the season
Continuous presence
Zero-base budgeting
Dayparting
exercises.explain: Spending follows demand. A light base the rest of the year (pulsing) keeps the brand in mind.

exercises.prompt: Total revenue 500,000 euros, total marketing spend 100,000 euros. What is the MER?
exercises.explain: MER = total revenue divided by total marketing spend. It ignores attribution quarrels between channels.

exercises.prompt: 200 new customers, 30,000 euros of total acquisition spend across all channels. What is the blended CAC?
choices: 150 euros
200 euros
30 euros
6,000 euros
exercises.explain: 30,000 divided by 200. Blended CAC includes all channels, paid and organic, which keeps everyone honest.

exercises.prompt: How do you prove that retargeting ads cause extra sales?
choices: An incrementality test with a holdout group
Reading the ROAS in the ad platform
Counting conversions after a click
Asking the platform account manager
exercises.explain: Retargeting shows ads to people who often buy anyway. Only a test with a group that sees no ads measures the true lift.

exercises.prompt: Marketing mix modeling needs individual cookies for each visitor to work.
exercises.explain: False. MMM uses aggregated data over time (spend, sales, seasonality). That is why it came back as cookies declined.

exercises.prompt: With zero-base budgeting, how is next year budget built?
choices: Every line restarts at zero and must be justified
Last year budget plus 5 percent
Half of what the CEO asks for
The same amount as the main competitor
exercises.explain: It forces you to question habits. It takes time, so many teams apply it to a few lines each year.

exercises.prompt: Put the steps of a media plan in order.
steps: Set the business goal and the target
Choose the channels and formats that reach that target
Set budget, reach, frequency and calendar
Launch with tracking and test groups
Read results and rebalance the budget
exercises.explain: Goal and target first, then channels, then the numbers, then measurement. Plans that start from the channel waste money.

exercises.title: The CEO wants to cut brand spend
exercises.scenario: A meal kit company spends 60 percent on performance ads and 40 percent on YouTube and posters. The CEO sees a ROAS of 6 on search and 0.8 on YouTube and wants to move everything to search.

steps.prompt: What is the flaw in comparing these two ROAS?
choices: Search captures demand partly created by the brand ads
YouTube ROAS is always computed correctly
Search ads have no effect on sales
Posters bring the most clicks of all
steps.feedback: Last-click platforms credit search for people who searched after seeing the brand elsewhere.

steps.prompt: How do you settle the debate with data?
choices: A geo test: pause YouTube in some regions and compare sales
Ask the YouTube rep for a better report
Survey 10 employees about the ads
Look at the likes on the YouTube videos
steps.feedback: Geo holdout tests measure incrementality across channels, without cookies.

steps.prompt: Sales drop 9 percent in regions without YouTube, and branded search falls too. Decision?
choices: Keep brand spend and optimise it, with MMM to set the mix
Cut YouTube anyway, the ROAS is too low
Move all budget to posters
Stop search ads completely
steps.feedback: The test shows brand ads feed demand, including search. Use MMM and tests to tune the split instead of guessing.

exercises.explain: Platform ROAS is not incrementality. Test, model, then allocate.
